rule:
Production master of the 168 clips: the frozen restrained rule validated
for Milo and Brittney (master_replacements.py / master_brittney.py) and
frozen for all four voices (NOISE_GATE_METHODOLOGY.md § Production freeze):
1. trim to speech (-50 dBFS envelope, 40 ms margin);
2. 10 ms raised-cosine fade at each trim edge — never past the speech
   onset: where a take starts with less than 10 ms before its first sound
   (the word already sounding at the file's first sample), the head fade is
   shortened to that margin, minimum 2 ms (click-free), so no initial
   consonant is faded;
3. outlier correction only: a clip more than 2 LU from the voice's median
   part/close level is moved just to the window edge; every other clip
   keeps its generated level (natural clip-to-clip dynamics; no per-clip
   LUFS forcing). Leads count too: a "Next." 9 LU under its part is an
   outlier, while the 1-2 LU softer "First." the founder approved in
   validation stays inside the window, untouched;
4. ONE voice-wide gain so the voice's whole 42-clip take reads -22 LUFS,
   the level of the founder-approved validation masters (comparable
   perceived loudness across the four voices);
5. peak safety only: the delay-compensated (5 ms) 4x look-ahead limiter at
   -2 dBFS, engaged only where a clip's true peak would exceed it;
6. 150 ms lead-in; 700 ms tail after a lead, 400 ms after a part/close;
7. AAC-LC .m4a, mono, 44.1 kHz, 128 kbit/s, written to
   assets/audio/guidance/<stable_id>/<fingerprinted manifest file name>.
No denoise, no EQ, no high-pass, no compression, no expander.
Also writes review sequences (as heard in THIRTY: a lead runs straight into
its part) to voice_production/listen/, the per-clip report and SHA-1s.
Usage: python -I master_production.py <repo>
